sections.prompt: Give one reason why you are learning German, then one condition for your next holiday.

sections.lede: Say each line aloud once. This section is not scored.

sections.title: Learning objectives
sections.lede: These are the three things you will be able to do by the end of the lesson.

sections.title: The big picture
sections.lede: Subordinate clauses with weil, dass, wenn and obwohl send the conjugated verb to the end.

blocks.text: A subordinate clause cannot stand alone; it explains or completes the main clause. The conjugated verb moves to the final position: Ich lerne Deutsch, weil ich in Deutschland studieren möchte.
Use weil for a reason, dass for a statement or fact, wenn for a condition or repeated event, and obwohl for a contrast. The main clause keeps normal word order, and a comma separates the two clauses.

blocks.title: Verb final, not verb second
blocks.text: In a subordinate clause the verb is last: …, weil ich müde bin. Do not use the normal second-position rule here.

sections.title: Rules & patterns
sections.lede: The patterns to keep in mind while you work through the examples.

rows: Ich bleibe zu Hause, weil ich krank bin.
Ich glaube, dass er recht hat.
Wenn es regnet, bleiben wir drinnen.
Sie geht joggen, obwohl es kalt ist.

items: The conjugated verb is the final word in the subordinate clause.
A separable prefix stays attached in a subordinate clause: …, weil ich früh aufstehe.
If the subordinate clause comes first, the main clause begins with its verb.

sections.title: Example sentences
sections.lede: Notice how the pattern behaves in a complete sentence.

items.de: Ich lerne Deutsch, weil ich in Deutschland studieren möchte.
items.en: I am learning German because I want to study in Germany.
items.note: Möchte is the final conjugated verb.

items.de: Ich glaube, dass er recht hat.
items.en: I think that he is right.
items.note: Hat is the final verb in the dass-clause.

items.de: Wenn es morgen regnet, bleiben wir zu Hause.
items.en: If it rains tomorrow, we will stay at home.
items.note: The main clause starts with its verb after the comma.

items.de: Sie kommt, obwohl sie krank ist.
items.en: She is coming although she is ill.

sections.title: Pronunciation
sections.lede: Short, focused sound work. Play each item and repeat it twice.

items.hint: The a is short and open: dahss.

blocks.text: German conversation values clear reasons, and weil is one of the most frequent conjunctions in everyday speech. A short “weil ich keine Zeit habe” is a complete and polite explanation.

In formal writing, da can replace weil at the start of a sentence. In speech, weil is more common, and in casual spoken German you may hear a second word order — but learners should use the standard verb-final pattern.

sections.title: Grammar spotlight
sections.heading: Subordinate clause word order
sections.lede: The conjunction opens the clause and the conjugated verb closes it.

rows: reason: Ich komme nicht, weil ich krank bin.
statement: Ich weiß, dass du recht hast.
condition: Wenn ich Zeit habe, komme ich.
contrast: Er bleibt, obwohl er gehen muss.

blocks.text: In a subordinate clause with a modal verb, the modal is the final conjugated verb and the infinitive sits just before it: …, weil ich arbeiten muss.

sections.tip: Say the subordinate clause out loud and stop on the verb. If the verb feels stranded at the end, the word order is correct.

sections.title: Choose the right answer
sections.lede: Choose the answer that fits the sentence or the rule.

exercises.prompt: Ich bleibe zu Hause, ___ ich krank bin.
exercises.explanation: Weil introduces the reason for staying at home.
The conjugated verb hat goes to the end of the dass-clause.

options: Ich lerne Deutsch, weil ich mag die Sprache.
Ich lerne Deutsch, weil ich die Sprache mag.
Ich lerne Deutsch, weil mag ich die Sprache.
Ich lerne Deutsch, weil die Sprache ich mag.
exercises.explanation: The conjugated verb mag must be at the end of the weil-clause.

exercises.prompt: Ich komme nicht, ___ ich keine Zeit habe.
exercises.explanation: The clause gives a reason, so use weil.
Dass introduces the content of the hope.

exercises.prompt: ___ ich Zeit habe, rufe ich dich an.

sections.lede: Click the words in the order that makes a correct German sentence.

exercises.prompt: Build: “I am learning German because I want to study in Germany.”
exercises.answer: Ich lerne Deutsch, weil ich in Deutschland studieren möchte.
exercises.explanation: The modal möchte is the final conjugated verb.

exercises.prompt: Build: “I think that he is right.”
exercises.answer: Ich glaube, dass er recht hat.
exercises.explanation: The dass-clause ends with the verb hat.

exercises.prompt: Build: “She is coming although she is ill.”
exercises.answer: Sie kommt, obwohl sie krank ist.
exercises.explanation: The verb ist closes the obwohl-clause.

exercises.prompt: Build: “I am staying at home because I am ill.”
exercises.answer: Ich bleibe zu Hause, weil ich krank bin.
exercises.explanation: The weil-clause ends with the conjugated verb bin.

sections.title: Speaking
sections.lede: Record or say your answer aloud, then compare it with the model.
sections.prompt: Give a reason for learning German, a condition for practising, and a contrast about your schedule.

model.de: Ich lerne Deutsch, weil ich in Deutschland arbeiten möchte. Wenn ich Zeit habe, sehe ich deutsche Serien. Ich lerne auch am Wochenende, obwohl ich oft müde bin.
model.en: I am learning German because I want to work in Germany. When I have time, I watch German series. I also study at the weekend although I am often tired.

tips: Put the conjugated verb at the very end of each subordinate clause.
Use a comma before weil, dass, wenn and obwohl.
Start with wenn to vary your sentence rhythm.

sections.title: Common mistakes
sections.lede: These are the errors learners most often make with this pattern.

items.wrong: Ich lerne Deutsch, weil ich möchte in Deutschland studieren.
items.right: Ich lerne Deutsch, weil ich in Deutschland studieren möchte.
items.why: In a weil-clause the conjugated verb goes to the end.

items.wrong: Ich glaube, dass er hat recht.
items.right: Ich glaube, dass er recht hat.
items.why: The verb belongs at the end of the dass-clause.

items.wrong: Obwohl es regnet, wir bleiben drinnen.
items.right: Obwohl es regnet, bleiben wir drinnen.
items.why: When the subordinate clause comes first, the main clause starts with its verb.
